**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

Article 12.3 already contains a robust, **mutual** insurance regime binding SFJ as well as PB:

- **12.3.1 Generally** — each Party carries insurance at its own expense with "A-" A.M. Best-rated insurers, primary and non-contributing, deductibles borne by the insuring Party, and **certificates of insurance on written request** (pre-signing and annually).
- **12.3.2 Minimum Requirements** — the greater of the Applicable Law minimum or the stated limits, covering **commercial general liability** (per-occurrence, products/completed operations aggregate, premises & operations, auto), **umbrella excess liability**, **clinical trials liability** (with post-termination tail), and **professional liability (E&O)** for subcontractors/Permitted Third Parties providing professional services.
- **12.3.3 / 12.3.4** — we receive additional-insured status on clinical trial liability and on product liability cover, and SFJ carries product liability post-Program Transfer.
- Additional protections in our favour: prior written notice of cancellation/non-renewal/material change, an express statement that insurance does not limit or reduce liability, and a flow-down requiring subcontractors to be insured.

This meets the preferred position on coverage types and certificate mechanics. Two points noted in the rationale rather than flagged:

1. **Limits are redacted** ([***]) throughout 12.3.2, so the USD thresholds cannot be verified from the document face — worth confirming against the unredacted schedule.
2. **No dedicated cyber/privacy line.** Personal data is instead handled in Article 11 (Intellectual Property and Personally Identifiable Information). Given this is a co-development/clinical trial arrangement rather than a hosting or data-processing engagement, this is a minor sub-element under the playbook's semantics.

Direction check: the clause is mutual and makes us an additional insured, so it benefits our party — no redline warranted.
